Future Work: Fine-grained sub-facial priors and annotations; video temporal aggregation and audio-visual fusion; learned/adaptive counter-forensics; certification bounds, low-light domain adaptation, and provenance + human-in-the-loop abstention
Keywords: attack-aware detection, counter-forensics, two-stream network, randomized test-time defense, weak localization, probability calibration, AURC, DeepFakeFace
Notes: Couples worst-of-K counter-forensic red-team training with a two-stream (semantic + SRM residual) architecture, 3-jitter test-time defense, and weakly supervised FPN heatmaps. Achieves 1.0000 AUC, low ECE (<=0.0196), and 0.9917 worst-case accuracy on DFF, though external SOTA baselines and cross-dataset tests are absent.

Title: Dual Frequency Branch Framework With Reconstructed Sliding Windows Attention for AI-Generated Image Detection
Authors: Jiazhen Yan, Ziqiang Li, Fan Wang, Ziwen He, Zhangjie Fu
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: ForenSynths (4-class ProGAN training); tested on GANGen-Detection, DiffusionForensics, UniversalFakeDetect, GenImage/AIGCDetectBenchmark, and AIGIBench (65 generative models)
Architecture: Dual-frequency branch (4-subband DWT window tiling + FFT phase-only) with Reconstructed Sliding Window Attention (LoAttention + GMLP) and ResNet-50 classifier
Task: Cross-generator AI-generated image detection (binary real/fake classification)
Explainability: Partial (qualitative DWT edge-residual and FFT phase-residual feature visualizations and logit distributions; no pixel attribution or textual XAI)
Generalization: Evaluated across 5 benchmarks and 65 generative models (GANs, diffusion, personalized diffusion, face-swap, social platforms); 92.1% mean Acc. / 94.1% mean A.P.; JPEG and Gaussian blur robustness tested
Limitations: Drops to 44.1%-52.1% on AIGIBench face-swapping and 54.6%-60.8% on social-media subsets; trails FatFormer on GANGen-Detection; binary only (no source attribution); general-image training
Future Work: Improve detection on unknown social-media generated images and face-swapping deepfakes; investigate CLIP-based performance differences on DiffusionForensics
Keywords: AI-generated image detection, dual frequency branch, DWT, FFT phase, sliding window attention, cross-generator generalization, deepfake detection
Notes: IEEE TIFS 2026 (Cited: 34). Unifies 4-subband DWT window tiling with FFT phase-only RSWAttention, achieving 97.3% (GANGen), 98.8% (DiffusionForensics), 96.4% (UniversalFakeDetect), 90.6% (GenImage), and 77.9% (AIGIBench) Acc. Strong relevance for MOD003/MOD004 frequency features, while exposing face-swap and social-media generalization gaps.

Title: Generalizable Synthetic Image Detection via Language-Guided Contrastive Learning
Authors: Haiwei Wu, Jiantao Zhou, Shile Zhang
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: ForenSynths (Tgan, 11 subsets), Tdf (46400 synthetic images + FFHQ with 5 anti-forensic/post-processing ops), Tfuse (800K train + 7 cross-domain test models), Twild (4000 platform synthetic + 2229 artist paintings)
Architecture: LASTED: ResNet50x64 image encoder + CLIP Text Transformer encoder trained with dual-axis main/secondary contrastive loss + frozen Linear Probe (also compared with ConvNeXt, ViT, MiT, NN)
Task: Generalizable synthetic image detection via language-guided contrastive learning (binary real/fake)
Explainability: No (only t-SNE feature visualizations; inference uses black-box linear probe without artifact localization or textual explanations)
Generalization: Evaluated across 4 benchmarks (Tgan, Tdf, Tfuse, Twild) covering GANs, DMs, Transformers, photos, paintings, and anti-forensics; achieves 0.974, 0.952, 0.913, and 0.941 AP; JPEG/blur/noise/resize robustness tested
Limitations: Not face-specific (Deepfake subset has lowest Tgan AP at 0.873); relies on noisy ClipCap captions; AP-only evaluation without thresholded/calibration metrics; heavy ResNet50x64 (4x A100); no source attribution

Keywords: synthetic image detection, language-guided contrastive learning, CLIP, linear probe, cross-domain generalization, image forensics, textual label augmentation
Notes: IEEE TAI 2026 (Cited: 76). Introduces LASTED with decoupled main (Real/Synthetic) and ClipCap secondary (Photo/Painting + caption) contrastive supervision, reaching 0.974 (Tgan), 0.952 (Tdf), 0.913 (Tfuse), and 0.941 (Twild) AP. High value for MOD004 specialist detector and cross-domain label design.

Title: Artifact feature purification for cross-domain detection of AI-generated images
Authors: Zheling Meng, Bo Peng, Jing Dong, Tieniu Tan, Haonan Cheng
Dataset: GenImage (1,331,167 ImageNet real + 1,350,000 fake across 8 generators: SD v1.4, SD v1.5, Wukong, ADM, BigGAN, GLIDE, Midjourney, VQDM); DiffusionForensics (40,000 real + 40,000 ADM train on LSUN-Bedroom; 1,000 real + 8 generators eval)
Architecture: Artifact Purification Network (APN): Swin-Transformer-tiny spatial branch with learnable orthogonal basis decomposition + dual ResNet-18 frequency branch with Hermitian-symmetric DFT suspicious frequency-band proposals and 8-head self-attention scoring + training-only CLUB mutual information variational estimator + MLP classifier
Task: Cross-domain (cross-generator and cross-scene) AI-generated image detection (binary classification)
Modality: Image (general scenes; spatial RGB + DFT amplitude/phase spectrum)
Explainability: Yes (Layer-CAM spatial heatmaps, t-SNE feature disentanglement visualizations, confidence-weighted frequency-band proposals and spatial reconstructions)
Generalization: Evaluated cross-generator on GenImage (80.4% avg Acc, +5.6% to +16.4% over 10 baselines) and DiffusionForensics (98.7% avg Acc, +1.7% to +50.1%), plus cross-scene ImageNet to LSUN-Bedroom (99.5% avg Acc, 0.1% drop)
Limitations: Accuracy-only evaluation (no AUC, AP, or F1); no post-processing or JPEG compression robustness testing; not evaluated on face-specific benchmarks; low GenImage accuracy on ADM (53.9%) and BigGAN (61.7%); dataset-dependent proposal count K; no parameter/FLOPs/latency profiling; no code URL in preprint
Future Work: Not explicitly listed in paper; implicitly post-processing robustness evaluation, face-forgery testing, automated proposal count K selection, and compute profiling
Keywords: AI-generated image detection, cross-domain generalization, artifact purification, frequency-band proposal, orthogonal decomposition, mutual information minimization, GenImage, DiffusionForensics
Notes: CVIU 2024 (39 citations; preprint PDF arXiv:2403.11172v1). Proposes explicit (DFT band proposals + spatial orthogonal bases) and training-only implicit (CLUB MI minimization) artifact purification. Strong cross-generator and cross-scene accuracy, though lacks AUC/AP metrics, compression robustness tests, and face-benchmark evaluation.

Title: PORI-Gate: Reliability-Guided Operator-Response Fusion for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
Authors: Hongxu Shen, Jin Tian
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: Training/Validation: ForenSynths 4-class (car, cat, chair, horse: 72,012 real/72,012 fake train, 800/800 val); Evaluation: CrossGen-38 (38 subsets from Diffusion1kStep, DiffusionForensics, ForenSynths test, GANGen-Detection, UniversalFakeDetect), UFD-aligned (15 subsets), GANGen-Detection/Self-Synthesis (9 GANs)
Architecture: PORI-Gate (11.77M params, 14.21 GFLOPs): 3 deterministic RGB operators (ColorQuant, LowBit, JPEGProbe) + shared ResNet18 encoder from scratch (256-D) + learnable operator embeddings + Reliability-Guided Fusion Gate (MLP + learnable global bias + temperature softmax + gate floor) + cross-operator context head (mean/max/std) + binary classifier
Task: Cross-generator and cross-dataset AI-generated image detection (binary classification)
Modality: Image (general scenes + face subsets; low-level spatial operator responses: color-space quantization residual, 3-bit low-order bit-plane, JPEG q=75 residual)
Explainability: Yes (per-image operator gate weights alpha_cq/alpha_lb/alpha_jpg, normalized gate entropy, deterministic operator response maps, frozen linear branch probes with 97.37% subset-level agreement)
Generalization: Evaluated zero-shot from 4-class ForenSynths across CrossGen-38 (92.86% mAcc, 96.94% mAP, 97.23% mAUC; 3-seed 92.39+-0.41% mAcc), UFD-aligned (95.62% mAcc, 98.01% mAP), and GANGen-Detection/Self-Synthesis (96.98% mAcc, 99.26% mAP)
Limitations: Degrades on Diffusion1kStep Improved-Diffusion (60.38% Acc, 67.64% AUC; reversed branch probes) and DDPM (76.37% Acc due to score-shift vs 90.16% AUC); no end-to-end post-processing robustness test across CrossGen-38; high sensitivity to inference-time normalization divisor mismatch; not tested on modern diffusion-face benchmarks (e.g., DiFF); no code URL reported
Future Work: Expand forensic cue coverage for challenging diffusion sources like Improved-Diffusion; improve adaptive allocation and cross-generator operating-point calibration/transfer
Keywords: AI-generated image detection, cross-generator generalization, reliability-guided fusion, low-level forensic cues, operator-response fusion, ColorQuant, JPEGProbe, CrossGen-38
Notes: IEEE Access 2026 (0 citations). Lightweight (11.77M params, 501.39 FPS end-to-end batch 32) reliability-guided fusion of 3 deterministic low-level RGB operators with real-only consistency regularization. Includes rigorous controlled ablations, 3-seed checks, and transparent Diffusion1kStep failure/threshold-shift diagnostics directly informing MOD006/MOD007/MOD008/MOD009.

Title: Bias-Free? An Empirical Study on Ethnicity, Gender, and Age Fairness in Deepfake Detection
Authors: Aditi Panda, Tanusree Ghosh, Tushar Choudhary, Ruchira Naskar
Dataset: DiffSynFace (40k+ synthetic faces from SD 1.0/2.0/XL/XL-Turbo, DALL-E 3, MidJourney, Adobe Firefly; 6 generators used in bias tests) + FairFace (ethnicity), CelebA-HQ (gender), Adience (age) real faces

Limitations: Pairs 4K DiffSynFace fakes with 3 mismatched external real datasets (FairFace, CelebA-HQ, Adience); omits FPR/FNR/AUC/statistical tests despite mentioning AUC/FPR; masks threshold miscalibration (e.g., DNF 50% ACC vs 81.5% AP); no intersectional or GAN evaluation

Keywords: deepfake detection, demographic fairness, diffusion models, DiffSynFace, out-of-distribution evaluation, ethnicity bias, gender bias, age bias
Notes: ACM Computing Surveys 2026 empirical fairness study claiming <5% demographic variation on DiffSynFace, though real-dataset confounding (FairFace/CelebA-HQ/Adience) and ACC-vs-AP miscalibration require caution alongside our DS0005 FairFace findings.

Title: Analyzing Fairness in Deepfake Detection With Massively Annotated Databases
Authors: Ying Xu, Philipp Terhörst, Marius Pedersen, Kiran Raja
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: A-DFD (4.7M labels), A-FF++ (8.5M labels), A-DFDC (4.6M labels), A-Celeb-DF (9.2M labels), A-DF-1.0 (38.3M labels) — 65.3M+ MAAD-Face annotations across 47 facial attributes (31 evaluated)

Title: Attention and residual mechanism-based CNN architecture (ARC-Net) with enhanced fairness generalization for deepfake facial image detection
Authors: Md Shihab Reza, Farhana Elias, Monirul Islam Mahmud, Nova Ahmed
Dataset: Hybrid 140k Real and Fake Faces + 500 Bangladeshi real faces (140500 total); Deepfake Dataset (142100); Deepfake Database (19457); 200 VIA-annotated XAI masks

Explainability: Yes (Grad-CAM and LIME; quantitative VIA mask localization: mean IoU 0.8396, mean Dice 0.9121, 88.9% peak-in-mask)
Generalization: Evaluated across 3 datasets (99% on hybrid 140k+BD, 97.60% on Deepfake Dataset, 99.33% on Deepfake Database) and 2 OOD cross-dataset setups (93.7%-94.2% in OOD-1; 92%-94% in OOD-2), plus South Asian subgroup fairness

Future Work: Extend to diffusion-generated faces and video temporal modeling; evaluate synthetic South Asian faces and multi-group fairness; test robustness to compression and social media perturbations; release reproducible code
Keywords: deepfake detection, ARC-Net, EfficientNetB0, attention residual network, fairness generalization, out-of-distribution, Grad-CAM, LIME
Notes: Strong relevant paper (2026): ARC-Net achieves 99% on 140k+BD, 92%-94.2% OOD cross-dataset accuracy, cuts South Asian real-face FPR from 22.0% to 10.0% (p=0.028, Brier 0.180->0.110) using <1% regional data, and validates Grad-CAM quantitatively (IoU 0.8396, Dice 0.9121). Lacks diffusion-model and compression robustness evaluation.

Title: Deepfake forensics analysis: An explainable hierarchical ensemble of weakly supervised models
Authors: Samuel Henrique Silva, Mazal Bethany, Alexis Megan Votto, Ian Henry Scarff, Nicole Beebe, Peyman Najafirad
Dataset: DFDC (5000-clip noisy test set from 128154-video corpus); Celeb-DF (OOD, 6229 videos); WildDeepfake (OOD, real-world internet videos)
Architecture: Hierarchical ensemble of Xception, Xception+Attention, and EfficientNet-B3+Attention with weakly supervised attention crop/drop augmentation (WS-DAN + Center Loss), Grad-CAM, 2D DFT, and 8x8 DCT Laplace beta analysis
Task: Explainable deepfake image and video forensics (binary classification + human-in-the-loop frequency verification)
Explainability: Yes (Grad-CAM on feature and attention layers + localized region cropping for 2D DFT and 8x8 DCT Laplace beta forensic analysis)
Generalization: Trained on DFDC (92.20% Table 2 / 92.4% Abstract, AUC 0.9752) and evaluated OOD on Celeb-DF (93.64%, AUC 0.9841) and WildDeepfake (72.73%, AUC 0.8079)
Limitations: Sharp OOD drop on WildDeepfake (72.73% acc, 15.82% FP); pre-diffusion scope only (no diffusion-generated faces); no temporal modeling (averages 10% frame predictions); missing training hyperparameters/code URL; qualitative-only XAI/DFT/DCT verification; no demographic fairness evaluation
Future Work: Improve OOD generalization on unconstrained wild videos and extend to diffusion-generated faces; automate and quantitatively evaluate secondary DFT/DCT forensics; add temporal video modeling; release code and full hyperparameters
Keywords: deepfake forensics, weakly supervised attention, CNN ensemble, Grad-CAM, 2D DFT, DCT Laplace beta, DFDC, out-of-distribution
Notes: Core system-design paper (103 citations): hierarchical forensic ensemble (Xception, Xception+Attention, EfficientNet-B3+Attention) with WS-DAN crop/drop augmentation, Grad-CAM region cropping, and 2D DFT + 8x8 DCT Laplace beta forensics. Achieves 92.20% DFDC / 93.64% Celeb-DF, drops to 72.73% on WildDeepfake; 60% of errors have <0.5 probability margin.

Title: Constructing New Backbone Networks via Space-Frequency Interactive Convolution for Deepfake Detection
Authors: Zhiqing Guo, Zhenhong Jia, Liejun Wang, Dewang Wang, Gaobo Yang, Nikola Kasabov
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: HFF (155k face images), FaceForensics++ HQ/LQ (120k sampled frames), DFDC (120k sampled frames), CelebDF (120k sampled frames)
Architecture: Space-Frequency Interactive Convolution (SFIConv) with Multichannel Constrained Separable Convolution (MCSConv) replacing vanilla convolutions in MobileNet, ResNet26/50/101, and VGGNet13/16/19
Task: Deepfake face detection (binary classification)
Explainability: Partial (Average Forgery Attention Maps / AFAMs visualize global vs local attention across 4/8/16 fake faces)
Generalization: Evaluated via leave-one-out unseen manipulation on FF++ HQ (TEST-DF/FF/FS/NT), cross-compression HQ/LQ on FF++, and cross-dataset DFDC<->FF++ and FF++->CelebDF

Keywords: deepfake detection, space-frequency interactive convolution, SFIConv, MCSConv, constrained convolution, cross-dataset generalization, manipulation traces, FaceForensics++
Notes: IEEE TIFS 2024 (cited=102). Proposes drop-in SFIConv + MCSConv replacing Body vanilla convolutions without adding parameters. Strong FF++ LQ resilience (96.47% AUC on SFIC-ResNet26) and DFDC (97.44% AUC), with public code, though untested on diffusion models and modest on CelebDF (71.0% AUC).

Title: FakeLocator: Robust Localization of GAN-Based Face Manipulations
Authors: Yihao Huang, Felix Juefei-Xu, Qing Guo, Yang Liu, Geguang Pu
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: CelebA (202599 real) + FFHQ (70000 real) + 7-GAN PNG set (STGAN, AttGAN, StarGAN, IcGAN, StyleGAN, PGGAN, StyleGAN2); DFFD; FaceForensics++; UADFV; Celeb-DF
Architecture: FakeLocator: DeepLabv3-ResNet101 encoder-decoder with Sigmoid limiting layer, Face Parsing Module attention, auxiliary CNN binary classifier, and L1 regression on gray-scale fakeness maps
Task: GAN-based face manipulation localization (full-resolution gray-scale fakeness map) and deepfake detection
Explainability: Yes (full-resolution continuous gray-scale fakeness prediction maps localizing manipulated facial regions)
Generalization: Evaluated across 7 GANs and multiple facial attributes, cross-attribute with face parsing, cross-method (FF++/StarGAN/StyleGAN/PGGAN) with real-only partial augmentation + single-sample clustering, and 4 degradations
Limitations: GAN upsampling-specific and untested on diffusion models; training requires paired real/fake images for partial manipulation ground-truth maps; single-sample clustering needs 1 labeled target sample; fixed 224x224 input resizing; code/custom dataset URLs not reported
Future Work: Visualizing per-image fake textures and classifying them by specific GAN and upsampling method; countering reconstruction-based evasion and non-additive adversarial attacks
Keywords: deepfake localization, FakeLocator, GAN upsampling artifacts, gray-scale fakeness map, DeepLabv3, face parsing attention, partial data augmentation, degradation robustness
Notes: IEEE TIFS 2022 (cited=145). Pioneering full-resolution gray-scale manipulation localization via GAN upsampling fake textures, face-parsing attention, and real-only partial augmentation. Strong DFFD/FF++ localization and JPEG/blur/noise/low-res robustness, though GAN-only and fixed at 224x224.

Title: Deepfake Media Generation and Detection in the Generative AI Era: A Survey and Outlook
Authors: Florinel Alin Croitoru, Andrei Hiji, Vlad Hondru, Nicolae-Catalin Ristea, Paul Irofti, Marius Popescu, Cristian Rusu, Radu Ionescu, Fahad Khan, Mubarak Shah
Dataset: Surveyed 24 datasets across image/video/audio/AV (Table 4) + proposed BioDeepAV (>1600 fake videos from EchoMimic, AniTalker, SyncTalk, GaussianTalker; >700 fake audio clips; real from HDTF & TalkingHead-1KH) + Celeb-HQ & FFHQ (generation benchmark)
Architecture: Survey & benchmark: generation (GAN, VAE, Diffusion, Transformer, NeRF, 3D Gaussian Splatting); detection (CNN, GCN/GAT, Transformer, Hybrid CNN+Transformer/RNN, traditional ML); BioDeepAV evaluated on StA, XceptionNet, F3Net, RECCE, TALL, UCF, MRDF
Task: Comprehensive survey of deepfake generation and detection + generative FID/speed comparison + OOD talking-face deepfake detection benchmarking
Explainability: Discussed (surveys explainable detection & artifact visualization; highlights uncertainty calibration and XAI as open gaps)

Future Work: Generation safeguarding & invisible watermarks; continuously updated OOD/open-set benchmarks; one-class real-only anomaly learning; explainable & uncertainty-calibrated detectors; POI detection with continual learning; multimedia blockchain provenance
Keywords: deepfake survey, deepfake generation, deepfake detection, out-of-distribution generalization, BioDeepAV, diffusion models, multimodal fusion, person-of-interest detection
Notes: Major 2026 ACM CSUR survey (61 citations) + BioDeepAV OOD benchmark. Shows >30% AUC collapse on diffusion/NeRF/3DGS talking-face generators, validates late fusion for modularity, and flags uncertainty calibration & XAI as key gaps.

Title: Towards Benchmarking and Evaluating Deepfake Detection
Authors: Jingyi Deng, Chenhao Lin, Pengbin Hu, Chao Shen, Qian Wang, Qi Li, Qiming Li
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
Publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
Dataset: 7 standard datasets (UADFV, DF-TIMIT, Celeb-DF-v2, DeeperForensics-1.0, FaceForensics++, DFDC, ForgeryNet) + proposed ID test set (976 fake / 2348 real videos; 25697 fake / 25697 real images across >=13 methods incl. FSGAN & MegaFS) with 5 perturbations
Architecture: Benchmark of 11 detectors (9 algorithms): HeadPose (SVM), FWA-ResNet50, Face X-ray (HRNet-W48-C), FFD (XceptionNet+Reg.Map), Multiple-attention (EfficientNet-b4), Xception, Mesonet-4, MesoInception-4, Patch-ResNet-Layer1, Patch-Xception-Block2, Conv LSTM (InceptionV3+LSTM)
Task: Fair, uniform-training benchmarking of deepfake face detection across detection ability, OOD generalization, perturbation robustness, complexity, and latency
Explainability: Discussed via knowledge-driven detectors (HeadPose landmarks, FWA resolution inconsistency, Face X-ray blending masks, FFD/Multiple-attention localization maps); no novel XAI method
Generalization: Extensively evaluated via cross-domain ID test set (51.2%-60.5% avg AUC vs 63.0%-97.2% in-domain) and 5 perturbation robustness curves
Limitations: Pre-diffusion scope (AE/GAN/Graphic only, no diffusion models); no ViT/SSL or audio-visual detectors; Face X-ray/FFD/HeadPose omitted on some large datasets; no repository URL in arXiv v2 PDF
Future Work: Evaluate Transformer/SSL and diffusion-era methods under uniform training; improve robustness to white Gaussian noise; combine complementary low-level/localization cues across accuracy-efficiency Pareto trade-offs
Keywords: deepfake benchmark, uniform evaluation, out-of-distribution generalization, ID test set, perturbation robustness, computational complexity, face forensics
Notes: Core 2024 IEEE TDSC benchmarking paper (49 citations; workspace PDF is arXiv:2203.02115v2 preprint). Re-implements 11 detectors across 7 datasets (92 models, 644 runs), proving no single detector dominates and all drop to 51.2%-60.5% AUC on human-vetted ID test set.
